newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says vets Gillette acquisition of Duracell.
newsitem.headline: EU says vets Gillette acquisition of Duracell.

text.p: The European Commission said on Monday it had been notified of the proposed takeover of U.S. battery maker Duracell International Inc by The Gillette Company, another U.S. company which makes shaving products.

It said in a statement to be published in the Official Journal that at first sight the $7 billion operation fell under the merger regulation 4064/89. The regulation bans creation or strengthening of dominant positions if they harm fair competition in the EU territory.
The Commission said the deal was submitted for clearance on October 4. It has about a month from that date to clear it or start an in-depth investigation.

The Commission in 1990 became the EU's clearing house for all major mergers and acquisitions. Although both Gillette and Duracell are non-European they do vast amount of business in Union which is why the deal must get EU clearance.
